key_insight: GatedLinear replaces the idea of forcing all time-series patterns through one model path with adaptive routing over complementary linear bases. This lets the model specialize on different temporal behaviors, such as smooth trends, drift, and recurring phases, improving flexibility for forecasting.
problem_solved: Traditional forecasting models often use one fixed computational backbone, which makes it hard to handle diverse and sometimes conflicting temporal dynamics in the same series. The paper addresses the challenge of modeling heterogeneous patterns without relying on a single inductive bias.
method: Builds multiple complementary linear bases to represent different forecasting dynamics.
Uses a gating mechanism to route each input toward the most relevant basis adaptively.
Combines the selected basis outputs to produce the final forecast with greater pattern-specific specialization.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more modular and adaptable forecasting design that can better handle real-world series with mixed behaviors. It may improve accuracy and robustness while remaining simpler than heavily stacked deep architectures.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing input time series routed by a gate into multiple linear experts
Side-by-side comparison of trend, drift, and seasonal/periodic patterns
Heatmap or routing matrix illustrating which basis is selected for different segments
Forecast vs. ground-truth line chart highlighting improved prediction quality
paper_title: GatedLinear: Adaptive Routing of Complementary Linear Bases for Time Series Forecasting
paper_authors: Qitai Tan, Ruiwen Gu, Yilin Su, Mo Li, Xu Lin
